variables.reason: The ledger variable Ra is defined in the problem as the first-order absolute moment of height fluctuations. The cited KB record pq_arithmetic_mean_roughness explicitly defines the arithmetic mean roughness (symbols Ra, R_a) as the mean absolute deviation of surface height from its mean level — which is exactly the first-order absolute moment described in the problem. The record’s si_dimension is given as L and its si_unit is m, directly supporting the candidate SI exponent vector (I=0,J=0,L=1,M=0,N=0,T=0,Theta=0): the quantity has length dimension and no electrical, luminous, mass, amount, time, or temperature dimensions. Therefore the candidate exponents are fully supported by the KB record.

The problem names kt as peak-to-valley height. The KB record pq_peak_to_valley_height defines mean peak-to-valley roughness height (symbols including k_t, kt) as a roughness-amplitude measure formed from vertical height differences between peaks and valleys. The record assigns SI dimension L (unit m), which corroborates the candidate vector (only L=1). The record’s definition matches the original problem’s meaning of kt, so the L-dimension and zeros for all other base exponents are justified.

The problem’s k_rms is the root-mean-square height. The KB record pq_rms_roughness_height defines root-mean-square roughness height (symbol k_rms) as the RMS fluctuation of surface height about its mean and lists SI dimension L (unit m). This directly supports the candidate SI exponents (L=1, others 0). The record applies specifically to surface-height statistics, matching the original problem context.

Sk is given as the skewness of roughness-height fluctuations. The KB record pq_height_skewness defines surface-height skewness (symbol Sk) as the third standardized moment of the surface-height distribution and gives SI dimension 1 (dimensionless). That record therefore supports the candidate exponents (all zeros) because standardized moments are dimensionless and the entry explicitly matches the variable name and physical meaning used in the original problem.

Ku is the kurtosis of roughness-height fluctuations. The KB record pq_height_kurtosis defines surface-height kurtosis (symbol Ku) as the fourth standardized moment of the surface-height distribution and reports SI dimension 1 (dimensionless). This directly matches the ledger variable’s definition and supports the candidate SI exponent vector of all zeros.

ES is the effective streamwise slope of the roughness. The KB record pq_effective_surface_slope defines effective surface slope (symbol ES) as the mean absolute gradient of surface height in a horizontal direction and explicitly notes that a surface-height derivative (length/length) is dimensionless. The record’s si_dimension is 1 and so supports the candidate SI exponents (all zeros). The record applies directly to the same physical quantity in the original problem context.

Po is surface porosity. The KB record pq_porosity defines porosity (symbols Po, P_o, ϕ) as the fraction of void area/volume and lists SI dimension 1 (dimensionless). The record’s domain includes surface porosity and its definition matches the problem statement. Therefore the candidate SI exponent vector of all zeros is supported.
